long_biography.plain_text:
Ray Catena entered automotive retail by opening Towne Auto Sales, a used-car and wholesale operation in Kearny, in 1958. Eighteen years later he moved into new vehicles with Ray Catena Chevrolet. In 1981 he sold that franchise and opened a Mercedes-Benz store in Edison, creating the luxury-dealership platform that became Ray Catena Auto Group.

The group expanded across New Jersey and New York through dealerships representing Mercedes-Benz, Lexus, BMW, Porsche, Audi, Jaguar, Land Rover and other premium marques. Catena remains its owner and president, while general sales managers lead individual stores and later-generation relatives participate across the enterprise. Those operational and family roles support the business without changing its founder-owned structure.

uncertainties.detail: Current Automotive News rankings identify Raymond Catena as owner, the 2024 state-industry profile names Ray Catena as president and dealership pages list separate store managers. Later-generation relatives participate in the enterprise, but no reliable public source establishes a completed ownership succession.

The 2024 state-industry biography dates Towne Auto Sales to 1958, while the current official group page says 1961. The biography uses 1958 because the detailed trade-association chronology names the business and Catena's age; the disagreement does not affect the founder or industry classifications.

Public trade reporting says Catena was 22 when he opened Towne Auto Sales in 1958, but it does not provide an exact birth date. Low-authority pages giving a precise date were rejected, and Kearny is treated as his hometown and business starting point rather than an established birthplace.
No identity-verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website was found. Organisational dealership accounts were not misattributed to Catena personally.
Exact-name and profile searches found no dedicated Ray Catena or Raymond Catena Forbes person profile. Articles mentioning the dealership or its owner do not satisfy the profile requirement.

Yacht-specific research, vessel facts, private-family trivia, allegations, legal matters, controversy, wealth estimates and dealership reviews were excluded and played no role in the classifications or biographies.
